title: Randomized execution as deterministic run on paired inputs
statement:
Let $p$ be a private-coin protocol with randomness spaces $\Omega_X$ and $\Omega_Y$, input spaces $X$ and $Y$, and output type $\alpha$. Then for all inputs $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$ and all coin outcomes $\omega_x \in \Omega_X$ and $\omega_y \in \Omega_Y$, the randomized execution of $p$ equals the deterministic execution of $p$ on the paired inputs $(\omega_x, x)$ and $(\omega_y, y)$:
\[
  \mathrm{rrun}(p, x, y, \omega_x, \omega_y) \;=\; \mathrm{run}\bigl(p, (\omega_x, x), (\omega_y, y)\bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: p a private-coin protocol over Ω_X, Ω_Y, X, Y, α
inputs x ∈ X and y ∈ Y
coin outcomes ω_x ∈ Ω_X and ω_y ∈ Ω_Y
replaced:
For any private-coin protocol $p$ and any inputs $x$, $y$, $\omega_x$, $\omega_y$, we
have $p.\mathrm{rrun}\;x\;y\;\omega_x\;\omega_y = p.\mathrm{run}\,(\omega_x, x)\,(\omega_y, y)$.
This is a definitional equality used as a simp lemma to unfold the randomized
execution to the underlying deterministic run.
